label: D2 after a2 led to S2 (common a2->S2 transition)
explanation: Fires only at D2, and only when the agent chose a2 and reached S2 through the common transition (in_action=2, in_state=2). Both are inputs observed at D2, so no future variables are used. Dev scores: precision 1.0, recall 0.9999, correlation 0.996. It never fires at D1 or GO, never after a1, and never on rare a2->S1 or a1->S2 transitions; state==2 alone gives precision 0.77. From the example windows (not checked quantitatively), magnitude looks highest (~0.95-1.0 of max) when a2->S2 follows recent a1 choices or comes just after a switch, and lowest (~0.65) in long streaks of rewarded a2->S2 trials. So magnitude may carry how novel or unexpected the choice is relative to recent history.

issues: The test split matches what was claimed: precision 1.0, recall 0.99997, F1 0.99998, mass recall 1.0, correlation 0.996.

Only 5 of the 158,603 active test steps fall outside the predicate, and they carry 0.0% of the activation mass. All are tiny (0.00-0.01): four at GO after a2 and one at D2 after a rare transition. This is scattered noise and there are no false positives.

Dropping either condition hurts. state==2 alone at D2 gives precision 0.77, and action==2 alone at D2 gives precision 0.74. So both action==2 and state==2 are needed, which supports the 'common a2->S2' wording.
The predicate uses no future variables: at D2 the agent has already seen its own action and the state it reached.

I did not check the magnitude claims (highest after a recent switch or a1 choices, lowest in long rewarded a2 streaks) quantitatively. The original explanation already says they were not checked, and the label does not rely on them.
